$comment: The one list of what changed in each AgencyOS version, newest first. CHANGELOG.md, the in-app What's new page and the release notes are all made from it (node installer/build/changelog.mjs). Add an entry here for every version; installer/VERSION must match the first one.

releases.title: Telegram accounts ship with the app, Qwen 3.5 models, and agent integrations
releases.summary: The Telegram account service now ships inside the installer, the accounts page shows every bot and account in one list, local AI picks Qwen 3.5 models for your computer, and an outside agent program can connect through a read-and-draft server. Nothing sends, joins or publishes without a person approving it.

changes.text: The Telegram account service is part of the installer: its own Python and the packages it needs, checked when the build runs. It starts with AgencyOS on this computer only. If it cannot start, AgencyOS still runs and the Telegram accounts page says so.

Telegram accounts at a glance: the Telegram accounts page lists the bots and accounts together, with ready, paused, limited by Telegram or needs-attention states, the reason, and when a limit ends. A limited account's work waits; it is never given to another account.

Qwen 3.5 for local AI: a 4B model for an ordinary laptop, a 2B model for smaller machines and a 9B model for computers with 24 GB of memory and 12 processor threads. Gemma models are still used for graphics cards that hold them and for small laptops. You can download any size by name.

Agent integrations (Admin → Agent integrations): connect an outside agent program through the AgencyOS server. Tokens are shown once, can be revoked, expire after 90 days by default, and are limited to ten working tokens. An agent with a read token can look things up; a draft token can only propose changes, and each proposal runs only when a person approves it in the app, under that person's role.

Agents never see client e-mail addresses or deal contact names, and no agent tool can send, schedule, approve, join, authorize, delete or run commands. The connection file format is not yet checked against each agent program's own documentation.

tips: Local AI is still optional. AgencyOS works without it.

releases.title: Antigravity by default, models you manage, templates, leads and a live dashboard
releases.summary: Antigravity CLI is now the default AI, so a new install downloads nothing; a local model is optional and you can download, try, start, stop and delete models yourself. Ads can be saved as templates, and the dashboard shows the live queue and the health of your bots and chats. Closing the window now shuts AgencyOS down (after telling you what that means) while minimizing keeps it working. A chat can also have backup bots, and the build can sign the installer as soon as a certificate is added.

changes.text: A brand-new computer needs nothing else. Everything AgencyOS runs on is in the setup file, and with Get ready to work ticked (the default) setup also downloads the local AI engine (about 1.4 GB, checked before it is used, no model) and installs Antigravity, so nothing is downloaded later. If you are offline or untick it, setup still finishes and Settings offers the same downloads.

Settings → AI and Copilot → Tools on this computer: Claude Code and Codex are downloaded only when you press Download, each with its own Windows installer, and the page says where from. Nothing is downloaded for them otherwise.

Every command-line tool signs in through your browser from a button (Sign in with your browser), never in a terminal. The tool opens its own sign-in page, AgencyOS notices when you finish, and you can cancel. Sign out is there for Claude Code and Codex.

Ad templates: in the campaign composer, press Templates to save the ad you wrote (text, media and link) or start a new campaign from a saved one. A template never sends anything by itself; the campaign made from it is reviewed like any other.

Compare versions of an ad: under the ad, choose Compare another version to write up to three more (B, C, D). Chats take turns, the preview has a tab for each, a reviewer approves all of them together, and Reports show delivery for each version. Clicks are still counted per campaign.

Repeat and drip schedules: post to each chat again and again (every hour to every year, up to 60 times, stopping at the end date), or start the chats one after another with a gap between them. The campaign page says in a sentence what will happen, and the jobs list names each version and repeat.

Live queue and bot health: the dashboard lists the posts that are sending, waiting or need someone (most urgent first), shows each connected bot with its state and chat count, and counts chats that are ready, lost or slowed down by Telegram. There is no shadow-ban indicator because Telegram does not report one.

Leads: create a link that opens one of your bots; whoever taps Start is added to your leads with the name and username Telegram gives, is told what is kept, and can send /stop to be deleted. Set status and notes, search, export CSV or JSON, or copy as text. Only people who asked are collected; nothing can message or add people in bulk.

Antigravity CLI is the default AI on the desktop app, and setup installs it. A new install no longer downloads a local model by itself; press Sign in with your browser in Settings → AI and Copilot, or pick another tool or an API key.

Settings → System → Local AI: download any model by name (with progress and cancel), try it, delete it after a confirmation, and start or stop the local engine. The automatic setup that picks models for your hardware is now a switch that starts off on a new install; an install that already used it keeps it on.

Closing the window now shuts AgencyOS down, after asking: no scheduled campaign is sent and no administrator's /authorize or /revoke is heard until you open it again. Minimizing the window keeps AgencyOS working in the background.
A command-line AI tool that quit before reading its question (for example because it was signed out) could crash the AgencyOS server with a broken-pipe error. It now reports the tool's own message.

Backup bots: on an authorized chat, choose Backup bots… to let other bots of yours post there too. Each must already be an administrator of the chat with permission to post; AgencyOS checks that live before every send, and nothing in AgencyOS can add a bot to a chat.

How the bots share the work: main bot first (a backup takes over only when AgencyOS cannot use the main bot because it is paused, removed or its token is rejected), take turns, or fewest posts in the last 24 hours first. You can also make a backup the main bot by hand.
Every change of bot is written to the audit trail with the time, the reason and the campaign, and delivery receipts show which bot sent each post.

The Windows build can sign the installer and AgencyOS.exe (Azure Artifact Signing, or a certificate file) as soon as a certificate is configured, and the test run checks that Windows accepts the signature. Setup steps are in docs/AGENCYOS_SIGNING.md.

A chat whose main bot is removed from it, or loses the right to post, is disconnected whatever backups it has, and a post that Telegram asks to slow down waits for its own bot. AgencyOS never switches bots to get around a chat's or Telegram's decision.
A backup that its chat stops letting post is taken off the list automatically, and that is logged.
Setup downloading the local AI engine no longer counts as turning automatic local AI on: a new install downloads no model until you ask.

Screens for Telegram accounts and communities (Settings → Telegram accounts, Grow → Communities): the plan is to sign in with the code Telegram sends, choose what each account may do, search the public communities and keep a directory of the ones you found with a recorded review of each one's advertising rules. The service that talks to Telegram as an account is not part of this release, so the screens say so and nothing is sent. It comes in the next release, and none of it has been tried against Telegram yet. Bots work as before.

A WhatsApp workspace under Grow, for people who agreed to hear from you: contacts with a record of how and when they agreed, imports that are checked before anything is saved, segments, message templates and one task per person. You open each chat yourself and send by hand; AgencyOS never sends a WhatsApp message and never says one was delivered or read. People who withdrew are kept out of every list.

notes: Telegram has still not been reached from the test machine: bots, backups and taking turns are tested against a simulated Telegram.

The setup downloads, the Download buttons and the browser sign-in use each vendor's own installer and sign-in page. They are tested here with stand-in programs; the Windows test run downloads Claude Code and Codex and starts a sign-in for real, but nobody can finish a browser sign-in in that run, so a complete sign-in has not been seen end to end. Antigravity's browser sign-in is the least certain: its documentation describes the first start opening the Google page, and AgencyOS starts it in a window nobody sees.

The local model manager and the new close-window behaviour have been run against a stand-in launcher and simulated engine; the Windows test run exercises them on a real machine. Antigravity, Codex and Claude Code themselves are not available to the test machine, so their sign-in and model lists have not been run for real.

The installer is still not code-signed in this release: signing needs a certificate that only the owner can obtain (docs/AGENCYOS_SIGNING.md). Even after that, Windows SmartScreen can warn for a while about a new publisher.
Auto-join, scraping members and bulk-adding people are still not built, and are not planned: see docs/AGENCYOS_RULES_CONFLICT.md.

releases.title: One app: Telegram bots and system settings live inside it
releases.summary: Connect as many Telegram bots as you need, from Settings inside AgencyOS. The separate status page no longer opens as a second app: what it offered (system status, local AI, where your files are kept) is now Settings → System, and the window starts on a plain start-up screen.

changes.text: Settings → Telegram bots: connect any number of bots by pasting each token from @BotFather. Rename, check, pause or remove each one. Tokens are stored encrypted on your computer and are never shown again.

Every chat is served by exactly one bot, chosen when you connect the chat ("Posts through"). Only that bot hears the chat's /authorize, posts its ads and answers in it, and the chat list shows which bot it uses. A paused or removed bot stops its chats with a clear reason; a chat is never handed to a different bot behind your back.

Settings → System shows what is running, the local AI, this computer and where your files are kept, with a safe way to change the data and AI folders (checked and confirmed first) and a Restart everything button.

The window opens on a plain start-up screen that says what is starting, then goes straight into AgencyOS. The launcher's own status page is no longer a second place to go: it appears only if something fails to start or while your data is being moved. The tray icon's "System settings…" opens Settings → System.

The Dashboard's Connect a Telegram bot button and the Telegram page now lead to Settings → Telegram bots inside the app. A chat cannot be registered until a bot is connected, because nothing could authorize it.
A bot Telegram stops accepting is marked Needs attention and no longer listened for; AgencyOS keeps listening for each bot separately, so a slow or silent bot never holds up another.
Settings → Storage is now part of Settings → System; old links to it still work.

notes: Real Telegram has not been reached from the test machine, so connecting and posting through several bots is tested against a simulated Telegram, as before. Telegram itself decides how many bots one account may create with @BotFather; AgencyOS sets no limit of its own.
A bot token that was saved in the settings file by an earlier version keeps working and appears as the Server bot. It cannot be edited in the app.
The new window start-up screen, tray entry and folder picker in Settings → System are checked by their logic and in a browser, not on a real Windows desktop.
The installer is still not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen warns on first run.

releases.title: An agent that does the work, and a window that feels like an app
releases.summary: The Copilot can now act as an agent: it looks things up, drafts work and proposes changes that you approve. Each AI job can have its own model and thinking level, the tools report their own models, and the desktop window loses its old title bar and heavy scrollbars.

changes.text: Agent mode in the Copilot (Ctrl+J, then Agent). It looks things up in AgencyOS (dashboard, clients, campaigns, Telegram destinations, approvals, reports, deals), writes ad copy, and proposes changes: add a client, create or edit a draft campaign, choose its Telegram destinations, submit it for review. You see each step as it happens and can stop it.

Every change the agent proposes shows exactly what will change and runs only when you press Approve, under your own role, and is recorded in the audit trail. The agent has no way to approve a campaign, schedule or send anything, delete anything or authorize a chat, so approval and authorized delivery cannot be bypassed.
Settings → AI and Copilot: a provider, model and thinking level for each job separately (ad copy, text improvement, Copilot chat, agent), each with its own Test button.

Claude Code, Codex CLI and Antigravity CLI are asked which models they offer and how hard each can think, so the lists follow the tools' own updates; local models say whether they can think at all. The model list has a Refresh button, and the thinking choices shown are the ones the chosen model supports.
A new thinking level, Extra high, for the models that offer it.
The window's own title bar is gone on Windows: the top bar drags the window and the minimise, maximise and close buttons sit on it in the colours of your theme.
Scrollbars are slim and quiet, with no arrow buttons, and only appear while you point at the area that scrolls. The sidebar scrolls without a bar and fades at the bottom when there is more below.
On the desktop app the Dashboard says plainly when no Telegram bot is connected and has a Connect a Telegram bot button, instead of talking about server settings.
Antigravity CLI is now kept up to date too, with its documented agy update. Claude Code and Codex CLI were already.
The Copilot's Ask mode is the same as before; Agent is the new mode next to it.

notes: Agents work best with a capable model. A small local model may not follow the agent's format; choose a stronger one for “Agent” in Settings. The agent was checked end to end with the real Claude Code, not with every provider.

Codex CLI's model list is read through its app-server, and Antigravity CLI's from agy models, from their published documentation; neither was run against a real install here, and each falls back to suggestions, with the reason shown, if it cannot answer.
Telegram delivery has been tested against a simulated Telegram, not the real one: no bot token was available to test with.
Answers and agent steps appear when complete; they are not streamed word by word yet.
The installer is still not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen warns on first run.

releases.title: One platform, one place for AI
releases.summary: A new look and layout that put every part of AgencyOS in one window, a Guide and feature explainer inside the app, and a single place to choose which AI answers: the local model, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity CLI or an API.

changes.text: A real top bar: where you are, a search that reaches every page, a light/dark switch, notifications and an account menu.

One sidebar for everything, grouped by the work: Workspace, Delivery, Grow, Social scheduler and Admin, with Guide and Settings pinned at the bottom. It folds to icons, and slides over the page on a small window.
Theme: light, dark or follow the computer. The last choice is applied before the page appears, so there is no flash of the wrong theme.
Search (Ctrl+K or ⌘K) works on every page, including the social scheduler, and also finds settings, guide pages and campaigns.

Settings → AI and Copilot: choose the provider (local model, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity CLI, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible service), the model, and the thinking level. A Test button says exactly what is wrong when something is not set up.
Copilot panel (Ctrl+J or ⌘J): ask how to do something in AgencyOS, or ask for a draft. It uses the provider you chose and never changes your data on its own.

Claude Code and Codex CLI are kept up to date automatically: once a day AgencyOS runs each tool's own update command, never at start-up and never while a request is using the tool. Turn it off, or press Update now, in Settings → AI and Copilot.
Model lists are read live from the provider (installed local models, your API account) so they do not go out of date.
A Guide for the main aim (create ads, get them approved, deliver to authorized Telegram chats, report), including how to set up a local model.
A feature explainer: every part of AgencyOS with what it is for, how to use it step by step, and what it needs.
What's new: the full change history of every version, inside the app and in CHANGELOG.md.
Ad copy, text improvement and the Copilot all use the provider you chose. When AgencyOS has to fall back to templates it now says why, and which model wrote the copy otherwise.
The search box no longer shows a second coloured outline around the field.
Notifications, the account menu and the search use the same icons, spacing and colours as the rest of AgencyOS.

The AI provider is chosen in Settings. Nothing is sent to an outside AI service unless you pick one there and save its key (on a server, AGENCY_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_AI=true is still needed too). An OPENAI_API_KEY in the environment is still read as the OpenAI key.
The old icon rail and the promotional links of the original scheduler are gone.
API keys are sealed with AES-256-GCM before they are stored, are never sent back to the browser, and are kept out of the audit trail. Only owners and admins can change AI settings.
Command-line AI tools run only inside the desktop app, in an empty scratch folder with their tools switched off and without AgencyOS's database or session secrets.

notes: AgencyOS 1.1.0 showed the version of Antigravity CLI but did not update it; 1.2.0 does. The bundled local AI engine is updated with AgencyOS itself, not separately.
Antigravity CLI support is experimental: it follows the programme's documented options, and some versions hang when another program starts them. Use the Test button before relying on it.
Answers in the Copilot appear when complete; they are not streamed word by word yet.
The installer is still not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen warns on first run.

releases.title: AgencyOS for Windows
releases.summary: The first release: AgencyOS by NextGen OS as a desktop app that runs entirely on your own computer.

changes.text: Windows installer that sets up the desktop app, PostgreSQL, Redis, Temporal and Node.js. Nothing needs to be installed first, and Windows Firewall is never asked.
Choose where your files live: a data folder and, optionally, a separate folder for AI models. Settings → Storage moves them later, copying and checking before anything is removed.
Local AI picked for your computer's memory, processor and graphics card, with a speed check that steps down to a lighter model if needed. It works offline once downloaded.
Clients, campaigns with a Telegram preview, four-eyes approval, optional client sign-off and a tamper-checked approved version.
Telegram delivery to chats whose administrators authorized the bot, with retries, backoff, a dead-letter list and a truthful status when something is not working.
Reports with CSV and print-to-PDF, tracked links, a sales pipeline, a knowledge base and invoices.
No sign-in: AgencyOS opens straight into your workspace on your own computer.
Rebranded as AgencyOS by NextGen OS, and released under a proprietary licence.

notes: Not code-signed: Windows SmartScreen warns on first run. The SHA-256 on the release page lets you check the file.
No automatic updates yet: install a newer setup file over the old one and your data is kept.
